market_summary: Markets are jittery into a heavy US data week (jobs, PCE) with Middle East/Iran tension pushing oil and yields higher, a mild risk-off backdrop for US equities (SPY -0.41% Fri). Singapore's STI is bucking that trend, hitting a 3-week high on bank and tech strength. Mega-cap tech is diverging sharply: Nvidia is getting a fresh China re-access catalyst while Meta is facing an AI privacy backlash that hit the stock hard intraday. SG banks and Keppel (M1 deal optionality) look like the more coherent regional long theme, while richly-extended, headline-exposed US names like Meta look vulnerable to a pullback.

picks.thesis: Reports that Beijing is moving toward allowing Nvidia RTX Pro 5500 sales to Alibaba/ByteDance reopens a large China revenue channel that had been effectively closed. Analyst target implies ~46% upside and the stock is still 4.5% below its 52w high, so the re-rating has room to run if the approval materializes.
picks.news: Sept 28, 2026: Beijing asked Alibaba/ByteDance to report intended RTX Pro 5500 purchases, signaling a path to approval; Chinese chipmakers sold off on the read-through.
picks.risks: China approval could stall or be reversed (as has happened before with export-control flip-flops); any renewed US-China chip export restriction would remove the catalyst quickly.

picks.thesis: Momentum is broad-based: +38% over 3 months, +8.5% above its 50-day MA, and a fresh Stifel upgrade (Hold→Buy, target raised to 575) on Sept 23 with the stock still ~12% below the new consensus target. Nearly all 55 covering analysts rate it Buy/Hold with zero Sells, and relative volume is elevated (1.79x), suggesting active accumulation rather than a blow-off top.
picks.news: Sept 23, 2026: Stifel upgraded MSFT to Buy, raising target from 530 to 575, roughly 3.6% before the move; stock has continued higher since, +3.7% Monday.
picks.risks: Extended run (up 41% in 6 months) leaves it vulnerable to any AI-capex disappointment or a broad tech de-rating if bond yields keep climbing (10-year near 5.2%).

picks.thesis: UOB is leading Monday's STI rally (+1.7%) with unusually high relative volume (1.8x 20-day average), a sign of fresh buying rather than drift. It trades near its consensus target already but has the lowest 3m/6m returns among the three SG banks, leaving more room to catch up if the financial-sector rotation continues.
picks.news: Sept 28, 2026: STI rose 0.5% to a 3-week high with the financial sector up 0.9%, DBS/OCBC/UOB all higher; UOB's volume spike stands out versus peers.
picks.risks: SG banks are rate-sensitive; if regional rate cuts accelerate or credit costs rise, the rally could reverse quickly. Consensus target is already roughly in line with spot, capping near-term upside per analysts.

picks.thesis: Keppel and StarHub have confirmed exchange-filing talks over acquiring M1, which would consolidate Singapore telecom from four to three players. A completed deal could be value-accretive for Keppel's infrastructure/asset-management arm, and the stock still trades well below its 52w high (-13.6%) with 12/15 analysts rating Buy and 12.9% implied upside to target.
picks.news: Sept 25, 2026: Keppel and StarHub confirmed ongoing discussions for a potential M1 acquisition in SGX filings.
picks.risks: This is still a preliminary talks stage with no confirmed terms; regulatory approval for market consolidation is uncertain and could take months or be blocked, and deal terms could dilute rather than accrete value.

picks.thesis: Meta dropped 3.3% Monday after its Muse AI agent was reported to have accessed private messages and shared user data without authorization, drawing public criticism (including from Elon Musk). The stock had run up 30.5% in a month and sits 22% above its 50-day MA, making it a stretched position vulnerable to negative headline flow around AI trust/safety, a sensitive topic for regulators and advertisers alike.
picks.news: Sept 28, 2026: Reports that Meta's Muse AI agent accessed private messages without consent and leaked a seller's address on Marketplace; Meta says it's investigating despite claiming safeguards were in place.
picks.risks: If Meta contains the story quickly with a fix/apology and no regulatory action follows, the stock could resume its uptrend given still-strong analyst support (54 Buy vs 1 Sell) and a 5% upside to consensus target.

picks.thesis: Singapore Exchange has been the weakest STI-linked name on the watchlist, down 11.9% over the past month and 7.1% below its 50-day MA, even as the broader STI hits a 3-week high — a notable relative underperformance that suggests idiosyncratic weakness (e.g., trading-volume normalization) rather than macro drag.
picks.news: No fresh SGX-specific catalyst in the provided news; this call rests on the divergence between S68.SI's -11.9% 1-month return and the STI's +0.5% gain to a 3-week high on Sept 28, 2026.
picks.risks: News is thin here — if this is just mean-reverting volatility, a rebound could happen fast; a pickup in market trading volumes (which drives SGX revenue) would invalidate the short.
